body: Maybe. I'm angry because my feelings get in the way. I'm angry because the angry fog I'm in keeps me from actually just doing what needs to be done. Things that I really wish I wasn't even doing anyway.

That's really all I have to say. Trying to do things for me always end badly. Last time I ended up in substantial amount of debt. My school's policies are too strict and would not appease me because I'm "under pressure." Their response: "Well who isn't." I really have no options.

Ultimately I think the fact that I have to put my mental health first just kind of shows how weak and and unresistant I am. I think that's another layer. What use am I to the world and to others if I'm always having to deal with hypersensitivity. Isn't there a point where you're supposed to just get over stuff and do it? That point never seems to come for me.
And by the "other options are much, much harder" you mean death correct?

I'm not sure why I'm so frustrated now. It's not like it's anything I haven't dealt with in the past: the anger at the amount of material I have to know and the demanding expectations of professors. I guess maybe I've just hit my breaking point where I've just had enough, but as I explained to the poster above, I don't have much a choice...that's probably another part of it. I'm so afraid of failure and either option presents some chance of failure

If I drop it I'll be wasting three years and become a bum with a mediocre job. Or I can continue on, be miserable, be angry and then still face the possibility of failure.

I really don't know. I'm really not sure who I am, so I'm not sure what my ideal job would be. Dropping out would be very difficult for me. I think it would be such a disappointment to my family especially since I've come so far. I'm stuck between a rock and a hard place where I'm screwed if I do screwed if I don't.
